newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX May COB electricity ends higher, May PV flat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX May COB electricity ends higher, May PV flat.

text.p: NYMEX May California-Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures settled higher, while May Palo Verde (PV) finished unchanged Monday, both contracts continuing to draw strength from short term factors.
Cooler-than-normal weather in parts of the Northwest resulted in higher than usual spot energy demand, and less runoffs for hydroelectric generation, market sources said.
Keen buying interest in COB and PV deliveries for this summer also provide psychological support for May values, brokers and traders said.
The return of the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 3 nuclear power unit near Phoenix, Ariz., to full output did little in dampening the firmness in the market, they said.

Reflecting higher short-term usage and tighter supply in the Northwest, day-ahead firm, peak electricity prices at COB firmed to $13.50-14.00 from Friday's 13.00-13.75, while those at PV held steady at $15.00-15.50.
May COB settled up 12 cents at $11.62 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a high of $11.90. June COB finished up four cents at $11.65. Other COB months ended nine to 25 cents higher.
May PV settled at $15.45, flat from Friday's settlement, erasing an early 35 cent gain. June PV finished down one cent at $16.53. Other PV contracts ended nine to 21 cents higher.
Brokers and traders said spot demand would slack off and rate of snowmelt would pick up when more spring-like temperatures return to the West.
"I do think it's short term. I don't see the fundamentals continuing to support this rise," said a Houston futures trader.
Separately, the 875 MW Intermountain coal-fired unit 1 in Utah was shut last Friday for maintenance, and expected to return to operation near May 6.
The 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 2 in central California was operating at 50 percent capacity this weekend after reconnecting to the grid Friday.
In the Pacific Northwest, forecasts called for temperatures near normal along the coast through much of the week and four to eight degrees below normal in the east.
Some clouds and rain were called for on Tuesday, then conditions were expected to dry out on Wednesday with more shower activity across the north later in the week.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be near to slightly above normal Wednesday then dropping to below normal levels for Thursday, Friday and Saturday.
Along with the lower temperatures, skies were expected to be cloudy in the latter part of the week, with a chance of showers and upper elevation snows.
NYMEX estimated 358 COB and 428 PV contracts were sold.
